newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan caretakers saved collapse - finance chief.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan caretakers saved collapse - finance chief.

text.p: Pakistan's finance chief said on Wednesday the caretaker government installed after prime minister Benazir Bhutto's sacking in November had saved the country from economic collapse.

"The economy was in a free fall and very close to the danger of a total economic collapse," caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid's adviser for finance and economic affairs Shahid Javed Burki told reporters in Karachi.

He denied criticism that the caretaker government had done nothing or that economic problems were insignificant before President Farooq Leghari dismissed Bhutto's three-year-old government on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.
"We have restored investor confidence, rebuilt forex reserves to a reasonably comfortable level and have stopped the outflow of capital," he said.

Burki said the caretaker government's major success was in lowering the trade deficit from an average $320 million a month to $160 million with exports showing a 20 percent rise in volume and a little less in value. Import growth had declined by four to five percent.

"Our most important achievement is that we have restored fiscal discipline where previous governments were not very careful in spending and loans were being handed over under bureaucratic discretion or political pressure."

However, Burki acknowledged that the caretaker government had not been able to speed up the privatisation of state enterprises, while foreign and domestic borrowing also remained a subject of concern.

But he said he had drafted a plan that, if followed by the next elected government, would result in the privatisation of all state-owned commercial banks by the end of 1997. Elections are due to be held on February 3.
Burki said Pakistan could lower debt servicing burden by using privatisation proceeds for retiring foreign debts.

"Pakistan has $60 to $70 billion worth assets and if only $10 billion of these are disposed off and used for retiring the most expensive posrtion of the debt, we would not have to worry about the rest of $25 billion which comprises of the cheap portion," he said.
